title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency
source_name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) - NIH
section: How much sleep do you need?
text: The NIH recommends that healthy adults need 7 to 8 hours of sleep per day. Sleep deficiency can interfere with work, school, driving, and social functioning. Long-term sleep deficiency is linked to an increased risk of heart disease, kidney disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, stroke, obesity, and depression. Sleep is critical for physical recovery, cognitive function, and hormonal balance, which directly impacts metabolic health and athletic recovery.
